title: Microprofile cheatsheet: throughput heuristics & quick runs
content:
Quick orientation:
- Purpose: a compact reference of short microprofile throughput experiments I ran while debugging a weird throughput cliff on small models (seq <= 128). Keep assumptions explicit and quickly repeatable.
- Target audience: me + any teammate who needs a fast repro for bursty small-request workloads.

Assumptions / harness:
- Model: opendelta-v1 (8-bit quantized), context: 64 tokens, response avg: 16 tokens.
- Hardware: g6-small (2xA10G-equivalent), single-GPU container pinned.
- Worker runtime: v0.9.3-local (kernel tuning flag: --batch-window-ms=6, --kv-cache=true).
- Client arrival: poisson and clustered bursts (see pattern ids below).
- Measurement: p50/p95/p99 latency (ms), qps measured at server ingress, token/s throughput, and observed batch sizes.

Test matrix (compact):
- Pattern A: steady poisson @ 120 qps for 120s
- Pattern B: spike: baseline 50 qps, sudden +300 qps for 10s, then cooldown
- Pattern C: microbursts: 8 requests every 200ms (sustained for 60s)
- Pattern D: synthetic shadow traffic (10% traffic duplicated, cold-KV priming)

Run notes + outputs (snippets):
--- run-A-poisson-120qps (2026-02-28T10:15) ---
mean qps: 118.8
median batch size: 1.4 (most requests single-request fastpath)
latency p50: 24ms, p95: 94ms, p99: 210ms
observed token/s: 19.6k
notes: stable, small variance. No queueing.

--- run-B-surge-+300 (2026-02-28T11:02) ---
baseline 50 qps -> spike to ~360 qps for 10s
server ingress qps peaked at 378 then throttled to 310 due to soft-cap
latency during spike: p50: 28ms, p95: 230ms, p99: 980ms
seen behavior: batch sizes jumped to median 6, but many requests hit backpressure and were serialized on slowpath. KV cache hit rate fell ~12% during spike.
consequence: tail latency dominated by cold-KV + batch serialization on worker.

--- run-C-microbursts (2026-02-28T12:05) ---
pattern: 8x every 200ms; avg qps sustained 320 but highly spiky
observed batch size distribution: 1 (44%), 2 (25%), 4 (18%), >=6 (13%)
latency: p50: 30ms, p95: 410ms, p99: 1250ms
server CPU: small cores saturated on scheduler thread; kernel wakeups correlated with p99 spikes
notes: microburst amplification due to wakeup and batching window misalignment (batch-window-ms=6 too small relative to arrival clustering).

--- run-D-shadow-prime (2026-02-28T13:00) ---
traffic: 10% shadow duplicates at 140qps baseline for 90s
obs: KV priming improved hit rate after 18s; p95 dropped from 160ms->85ms once prime warmed. Prefill strategy (cold-shadow prewarm for 30s) shows dramatic p99 improvement in next runs.

Quick heuristics (takeaway bullets):
1) For microburst-heavy patterns, slightly increasing batch-window to 10-12ms reduced p95 by ~45% in repeated A/B runs, because it allowed more natural coalescing without long serialization.
2) If KV hit-rate drops during spikes, consider a tiny warmup shadow for small models (10-30s) as a cheap mitigation.
3) Backpressure serialization happens when worker queue length exceeds batchable capacity; heuristic: if median batch size > 4 and p99 > 700ms, force a local shed or route to dedicated pool.
4) Kernel-wakeup noise is visible on small machines; moving scheduler pin from core0->core2 reduced jitter in later microbench.

Small checklist to reproduce locally: (commands shorthand)
- build runtime: ./scripts/build-local --image=local:0.9.3 --flags='--batch-window-ms=6 --kv-cache'
- launch one worker: docker run --cpuset-cpus=0,1 -e MODEL=opendelta-v1 local:0.9.3
- run harness: ./tools/perf-generator --pattern microburst --clients 8 --duration 120 --qps 320
- capture traces: export PERF_TRACE=1; collect /tmp/perf-<ts>.json

Open questions / next probes:
- Can we instrument and surface per-request KV priming state in tracing so that we can correlate p99 directly with 'kv-primed' boolean? (ticket candidate)
- Evaluate whether increasing batch-window to 10ms hurts steady-state median latency for small single-request workloads — quick A/B needed.
- Try pluggable prefill policy: 10% shadow warm for the first 30s after model load; measure cost tradeoff (extra tokens) vs tail latency improvement.

Action items (short):
- [ ] Create INF ticket for KV-priming trace flag (INF-2892) — assign Arjun
- [ ] Run A/B of batch-window 6ms vs 10ms with steady poisson @120qps + microburst overlay; gather p99 over 6 runs — assign Inez
- [ ] Small PR to allow scheduler cpu pinning via env var in local container runtime — draft branch: github.com/redwood/inference/tree/scheduler-cpu-pin-miles

Quick TL;DR (1-liner): microbursts + small-context models -> wakeup jitter + KV cold misses amplify p99; small increase to batch coalescing + light shadow prefill is an inexpensive mitigation path worth A/B testing.

Raw attachments referenced in harness (local): /tmp/perf-20260228-1015.json (run A), /tmp/perf-20260228-1102.json (run B)

Notes to self: push clean reproducer script to tools/perf-generator and add `--shadow-prefill` flag so infra can repro shadow priming easily.

End of page.
